rounds.text: RIR Power Electronics Ltd trades at an astronomical price-to-earnings ratio of 187x according to filed statements, dramatically higher than the sector benchmark of 37.8x [E1, E6]. This extreme valuation is entirely disconnected from the company's recent operational reality, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of -19% and flat 0% compounded profit growth over the past three years [E20, E21]. Furthermore, the stock sits merely 10% of the way up its 52-week range of 132 low to 388 high, signaling intense downward market pressure despite the lofty multiple [E5]. Compounded profitability over longer periods shows stagnation in the near term, reinforced by a negative year-on-year sales decline of 9% [E69]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong historical multi-year performance with a 10-year compounded profit growth of 22% and a 5-year growth rate of 38% [E18, E19]. Ultimately, paying a price-to-book ratio of 8.93x against a meager return on assets of 3.66% exposes investors to severe multiple-contraction risks [E2, E8].
